testimony.witness_title: unknown (likely attorney or California organization representative)
testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Status of Court of Claims suit for California Indians; opposition to private attorneys for California Indians; history of Jurisdictional Act
testimony.key_claims: Suit is practically ready for hearing before Court of Claims; delays due to getting information from Government bureaus and taking turn among similar cases; recovery was contemplated at $6-10 million when bill was formulated; bill was purposely framed to have attorney general represent Indians to avoid competition among organizations and contingent fee claims; there is no controverted matter, mostly computation; land value was fixed at $1.25 per acre; per capita distribution is contrary to bill's intent; at time of bill passage there were three Indian associations in California (Collett's, Tibbitts', and Indian Defense Association); California itself has real interest in Indian rehabilitation; he was part of one of those organizations and did not want fight over attorneyship; no proposal for compromise of which he is aware

testimony.witness_title: Executive Representative, Indians of California, Inc.
testimony.hearing: Subcommittee hearing at St. Francis Hotel
testimony.location: St. Francis Hotel, San Francisco, California
testimony.subject: California Indian claims; conduct of attorney general; history of jurisdictional act; activities of John Collier; character of various witnesses
testimony.key_claims: Stephen Knight was delegate for Indians of California in 1922 then switched to Indian Brotherhood and Kahn bill; John Collier gave Knight $250 to organize Indian Brotherhood; William Fuller also switched sides; F. G. Collett's indictment related to Rellimeo Film Syndicate had nothing to do with Indian affairs and was dismissed; attorney general has been damagingly derelict; attorney general filed suit 15 months late causing other cases to be filed ahead; attorney general's petition had multiple errors including failing to include many tribes; attorney general failed to amend petition for additional 2 years 7 months; amendments included new parties and new subject matter filed 10 months after jurisdiction expired; attorney general wrongfully relied on defendant to prepare plaintiff's case; Indians need private attorneys; Indians of California Inc. was regularly incorporated and recognized by California courts; financial reports will show Collett was without compensation for years and is owed over $10,000; Commissioner misled Congressional committees and sought predetermined settlement of $6 million
